summary: This Dockerfile creates a Docker image based on Ubuntu 24.04 with zsh shell, git, and curl installed. It then installs Oh-My-Zsh (a zsh configuration framework), adds the zsh-autosuggestions plugin to provide command hints, pre-populates shell history with common docker commands, and customizes the shell prompt with a whale emoji to indicate you're in a container.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to skip interactive prompts by setting the frontend to 'noninteractive', so the installation won't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so if any step fails, the whole thing stops — and we update the package list before installing anything to ensure we get current versions.
explanations.11: After installing packages, we delete the apt cache files to shrink the image size, since we won't need them again inside this container.
explanations.14: This runs the Oh-My-Zsh installer script from the internet, with the --unattended flag so it doesn't ask questions, and --keep-zshrc so it doesn't overwrite any existing shell config.
explanations.20: The sed command finds the line that says plugins=(git) and replaces it with plugins=(git zsh-autosuggestions), effectively adding the autosuggestions plugin to the active plugins list.
explanations.24: We're writing hardcoded shell history entries in a special format (with fake timestamps) so that when you start typing 'docker' in the shell, zsh can suggest previous commands from this pre-filled history.
explanations.33: This sets the default command to run when the container starts — it launches zsh in interactive mode (-i) with a login shell (-l), so you get a normal shell prompt.
